words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.tr:
n. 赞助商；
v. 赞助；
words.ex: The company is a sponsor of the football match.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是这场足球赛的赞助商。
words.en: A sponsor is a person or organization that pays for or contributes to the costs involved in staging a sporting or artistic event in return for advertising. A sponsor can also be someone who introduces and supports a proposal for a new law.

words.tr: adj. 自发的；自然产生的；
words.ex: The children gave a spontaneous cheer.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们自发地欢呼起来。
words.en: Something that is spontaneous is not planned but happens or is done because of a sudden impulse or natural feeling.

words.ex: She poured tea from the pot.
words.ex_cn: 她从壶里倒出了茶。
words.en: A pot is a deep round container used for cooking.

words.tr:
n. 地点；场所；斑点；
v. 发现；识别；
words.ex: This is the spot where we met for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们第一次见面的地方。
words.en: A spot is a particular place or point. It can also refer to a small mark or stain, or a small amount of something. As a verb, it means to see, notice, or recognize someone or something.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.ex: The staff at the hotel are very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的职员非常友好。
words.en: The people who work for a particular organization or company, or a group of officers assisting a commanding officer.

words.tr:
n. 东西；原料；
v. 塞；填充；
words.ex: I need to clean up all this stuff.
words.ex_cn: 我需要清理这些东西。
words.en: If you stuff something somewhere, you push it there quickly and roughly. If you stuff a container or space with something, you fill it completely with that thing.

words.tr:
n. 材料；原料；
adj. 物质的；
words.ex: The table is made of wood material.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是由木头材料制成的。
words.en: Material refers to the substance or substances from which a thing is made or can be made, or information or ideas for use in creating a book or other work.

words.tr:
n. 污点；
v. 玷污；
words.ex: There is a coffee stain on the table.
words.ex_cn: 桌子上有一个咖啡污点。
words.en: A stain is a mark on something that is difficult to remove, especially one made by a liquid such as blood or coffee. To stain something means to leave a mark on it that is difficult to remove.

words.ex: He put the letter in an envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他把信装进了一个信封。
words.en: An envelope is a flat, usually rectangular or square, paper container for a letter, which you seal before you send it by post.

words.tr:
v. 粘附；（随意）放置；忍受；
n. 棍枝；条状物；球棍；
words.ex: The glue makes the paper stick to the table.
words.ex_cn: 胶水使纸粘在桌子上。
words.en: A stick is a thin branch which has fallen off a tree. If you stick something somewhere, you put it there in a rather casual way.

words.ex: He adheres to his principles even when it's hard.
words.ex_cn: 即使很难，他仍然坚持自己的原则。
words.en: If you adhere to a rule or agreement, you act in the way that it says you should.

words.ex: Please attach the file to the email.
words.ex_cn: 请将文件附加到邮件中。
words.en: To attach something to something else means to fasten or join it to the other thing.

words.ex: He cooks soup on the stove.
words.ex_cn: 他用炉子煮汤。
words.en: A stove is a piece of equipment which provides heat, either for cooking or for heating a room.

words.tr:
adv. 径直；直接；直；
adj. 直的；
words.ex: He walked straight to the door.
words.ex_cn: 他径直走向门。
words.en: extending or moving uniformly in one direction only; without a curve or bend.

words.ex: The cow eats straw from the barn.
words.ex_cn: 牛吃谷仓里的稻草。
words.en: A straw is a thin tube of paper or plastic that you use to suck a drink into your mouth.

words.tr:
n. 压力；强调；
v. 着重；强调；
words.ex: He feels stress from too much work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为工作太多而感到压力。
words.en: Stress is a state of mental or emotional strain or tension resulting from adverse or demanding circumstances.

words.ex: He felt great distress when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到非常忧虑。
words.en: Distress is a feeling of extreme worry, sadness, or pain.

words.tr:
n. 袭击；罢工；
v. 击打；侵袭；突然想到；
words.ex: The strike on the base happened at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 对基地的袭击发生在黎明时分。
words.en: To hit someone or something forcefully; to stop work as a form of protest.

words.tr:
v. 击；撞；
n. 撞击；敲击；
words.ex: He knock on the door.
words.ex_cn: 他敲了敲门。
words.en: To strike a surface noisily to attract attention, especially when waiting to be let in through a door.

words.tr:
v. 努力；斗争；挣扎；
n. 努力；斗争；难事；
words.ex: He struggles to finish his homework every night.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上都努力完成作业。
words.en: If you struggle to do something, you try hard to do it, even though it is difficult or other people are making it difficult for you.

words.ex: He is stubborn and won't change his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他很顽固，不肯改变主意。
words.en: Someone who is stubborn is determined to do what they want and is very unwilling to change their mind.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.tr:
adj. 抽象的；非具体的；
n. 摘要；概要；抽象派艺术作品；
words.ex: The painting shows an abstract shape.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画展示了一个抽象的形状。
words.en: An abstract idea or way of thinking is based on general ideas rather than on real things and events.

words.ex: The bright flowers attract bees.
words.ex_cn: 鲜艳的花朵吸引蜜蜂。
words.en: If something or someone attracts you, they have particular qualities which cause you to like or admire them.

words.ex: She is an attractive woman.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有吸引力的女性。
words.en: An attractive person or thing is pleasing or appealing to look at.

words.ex: The farmer drives a tractor in the field.
words.ex_cn: 农夫在田里开拖拉机。
words.en: A tractor is a powerful motor vehicle with large rear wheels, used chiefly on farms for hauling equipment and trailers.

words.ex: Subtract 5 from 10 to get 5.
words.ex_cn: 从10中减去5得到5。
words.en: If you subtract one number from another, you take the first number away from the second.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.ex: Two countries signed a treaty to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 两个国家签署了一项条约以停止战争。
words.en: A treaty is a formal agreement between two or more countries or groups, especially one that is written down and signed by their leaders.

words.tr:
v. 适合；相配；
n. 套装；西装；诉讼；
words.ex: This color suits her well.
words.ex_cn: 这个颜色很适合她。
words.en: A suit is a set of clothes made from the same fabric, usually consisting of a jacket and trousers or a skirt. As a verb, to suit means to be appropriate or acceptable for someone or something.

words.ex: She bought a new garment for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一件新衣服。
words.en: A garment is a piece of clothing; used especially in contexts where you are talking about the manufacture or sale of clothes.

words.ex: He packed his clothes into a suitcase.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服装进了行李箱。
words.en: A suitcase is a case with a handle and often with wheels, used for carrying clothes and possessions when travelling.

words.ex: They booked a hotel suite for their honeymoon.
words.ex_cn: 他们为蜜月预订了一间酒店套房。
words.en: A set of rooms designated for use together, especially in a hotel; a set of musical compositions designed to be performed in a sequence.

words.ex: He gave a summary of the story at the end.
words.ex_cn: 他在结尾对故事做了总结。
words.en: A summary is a brief statement or account of the main points of something.

words.ex: He learned a new technique to paint better.
words.ex_cn: 他学了一种新的绘画技术。
words.en: A technique is a particular method of doing an activity, usually a method that involves practical skills.

words.ex: He works in a technical department.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个技术部门工作。
words.en: Technical means involving the sorts of machines, processes, and materials that are used in industry, transport, and communications.

words.ex: New technology helps farmers grow more food.
words.ex_cn: 新技术帮助农民种植更多的粮食。
words.en: Technology refers to the application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry.

words.ex: The ancient temple stands on the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的庙宇矗立在山上。
words.en: A temple is a building used for the worship of a god or gods in some religions.

words.ex: He took a temporary job during summer.
words.ex_cn: 他在暑假期间做了一份短暂的工作。
words.en: Something that is temporary lasts for only a limited time.

words.tr: adj. 现代的；当代的；同时代的；
words.ex: This museum displays contemporary art.
words.ex_cn: 这个博物馆展示现代艺术。
words.en: Belonging to or occurring in the present; or a person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.

words.ex: The bus stops at the terminal at 9 PM.
words.ex_cn: 公交车晚上9点到达终点站。
words.en: A terminal is a place where vehicles, passengers, or goods begin or end a journey. It can also refer to a computer device at which a user enters data or commands.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: The thief stole a wallet from the bag.
words.ex_cn: 小偷偷走了包里的钱包。
words.en: A thief is a person who steals something from another person or place.

words.ex: He stole a book from the store.
words.ex_cn: 他从商店偷了一本书。
words.en: To take something that belongs to someone else without their permission and without intending to return it.

words.ex: The burglar broke into the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 窃贼在夜里闯入了房子。
words.en: A burglar is a person who illegally enters buildings and steals things.

words.ex: The robot cleans the floor every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个机器人每天打扫地板。
words.en: A robot is a machine that is programmed to move and perform certain tasks automatically.

words.ex: The thieves robbed the bank last night.
words.ex_cn: 小偷昨晚抢劫了银行。
words.en: To rob someone or somewhere means to take money or property illegally from them, often using force.

words.tr:
v. 无所事事；闲荡
adj. 懈怠的；闲散的；不做事的
words.ex: He idles away the whole afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他整个下午都无所事事。
words.en: If you describe someone as idle, you mean they are not doing anything or they are not working hard.

words.tr:
adj. 疲倦的；厌烦的
v. （使）厌倦；厌烦
words.ex: He looked weary after working all day.
words.ex_cn: 他工作了一整天后看起来很疲惫。
words.en: If you are weary, you are very tired.

words.tr:
v. 耗尽；用完；使筋疲力尽
n. 排气管；废气
words.ex: The long hike exhausted him.
words.ex_cn: 这次漫长的徒步旅行让他筋疲力尽。
words.en: If something exhausts you, it makes you so tired, either physically or mentally, that you have no energy left.

words.tr: adj. 疲倦的；厌烦的； v. “tire”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt tired after running for an hour.
words.ex_cn: 他跑了一个小时后感到疲倦。
words.en: If you are tired, you feel that you want to rest or sleep.

words.ex: The car has a flat tyre.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有一个瘪了的轮胎。
words.en: A tyre is a thick piece of rubber which is fitted onto the wheels of vehicles such as cars, buses, and bicycles in order to make them move smoothly and safely.

words.ex: He reads books in his leisure.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间读书。
words.en: Leisure is the time when you are not working and you can relax and do things that you enjoy.

words.ex: He will retire next year.
words.ex_cn: 他明年将退休。
words.en: If you retire, you stop working, usually because you have reached a certain age or because you are ill.

words.tr: adj. 全部的；整个的；完全的；
words.ex: He ate the entire cake.
words.ex_cn: 他吃掉了整个蛋糕。
words.en: You use entire to emphasize that you are referring to the whole of something, for example, the whole of a place, time, or population.

words.ex: He is thirsty after running.
words.ex_cn: 他跑步后口渴了。
words.en: If you are thirsty, you feel a need to drink something.

words.ex: The children starve without food.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们没有食物就会挨饿。
words.en: To suffer or die from lack of food.

words.ex: He felt hunger after running for an hour.
words.ex_cn: 他跑了一个小时后感到饥饿。
words.en: A strong desire or need for food.

words.ex: He hunts deer in the forest every autumn.
words.ex_cn: 他每年秋天在森林里打猎。
words.en: To hunt means to chase and try to catch or kill animals for food or sport.

words.ex: The children are eager to open their presents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们渴望打开他们的礼物。
words.en: If you are eager to do or have something, you want to do or have it very much.

words.ex: The eagle flies high above the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 鹰在山上面高飞。
words.en: A large bird of prey with a massive hooked bill and long broad wings, known for its keen sight and powerful soaring flight.

words.tr:
n. 安逸；轻松；
v. 缓解；减轻；
words.ex: He enjoys the ease of living in a quiet village.
words.ex_cn: 他享受住在安静村庄里的安逸。
words.en: If you talk about the ease of a particular activity, you are referring to the way that it has been made easier to do, or to the fact that it is already easy to do. Ease is also a state of being comfortable and without worry or anxiety.

words.ex: He can solve the problem easily.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易就能解决这个问题。
words.en: Without difficulty or effort.

words.ex: Children hunt eggs on Easter morning.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在复活节早上找鸡蛋。
words.en: Easter is a Christian festival and holiday celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ on the third day after his crucifixion at Calvary as described in the New Testament.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.ex: The book has a long title.
words.ex_cn: 这本书有一个很长的标题。
words.en: A title is a name that describes someone's position or job, or a word or phrase that is used to describe a book, film, play, etc.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.tr:
n. 率；速度；比率；价格；费用；
v. 被评价；定级；（被）认为；
words.ex: The interest rate is very low this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年的利率非常低。
words.en: A rate is the speed at which something happens or changes, or the amount or number of something that happens or changes in a particular period.

words.tr:
n. 速度；速率；
v. 加速；加快；
words.ex: The car's speed was too high on the wet road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在湿滑路面上的速度太快了。
words.en: Speed is the rate at which something moves or happens.

words.ex: He exaggerates his achievements to impress others.
words.ex_cn: 他夸张自己的成就来给别人留下印象。
words.en: If you exaggerate, you indicate that something is, for example, worse or more important than it really is.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.ex: I can't tolerate loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 我无法容忍巨大的噪音。
words.en: If you tolerate a situation or person, you accept them although you do not particularly like them.

words.tr:
n. 酷刑；拷打
v. 拷打；折磨
words.ex: The prisoner suffered from torture during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯在战争期间遭受了酷刑。
words.en: Torture is the act of deliberately inflicting severe physical or psychological pain on someone, typically to extract information or a confession, or as a punishment.

words.tr:
n. 熊；
v. 承受；忍受；带有；生（孩子）；
words.ex: A bear walked near the campsite.
words.ex_cn: 一只熊在露营地附近走动。
words.en: If you bear something, you accept it and are able to deal with it, even though it is unpleasant or painful. A bear is a large, strong wild animal with thick fur and sharp claws.

words.ex: He grew a thick beard last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天他留了一脸浓密的胡须。
words.en: The hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks.

words.tr:
n. 眼泪；泪水；
v. 撕裂；撕开；
words.ex: A tear fell down her cheek when she heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当她听到这个消息时，一滴眼泪从脸颊滑落。
words.en: A tear is a drop of clear salty liquid that is produced by the glands in your eyes when you cry or when your eyes are irritated.

words.tr: n. 旅游；游览；巡回活动；
words.ex: We went on a tour of Paris last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天我们去巴黎旅游了。
words.en: A tour is a journey in which you visit several places that interest you, especially on holiday.

words.ex: The tourist took photos at the museum.
words.ex_cn: 这位旅游者在博物馆拍照。
words.en: A tourist is a person who is visiting a place for pleasure and interest, especially when they are on holiday.

words.ex: He won the chess tournament last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周赢得了国际象棋锦标赛。
words.en: A tournament is a competition in which players who win a match continue to play further matches in the competition until just one person or team is left.

words.tr:
n. 旅行；旅程；
v. 绊倒；
words.ex: We went on a trip to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山里旅行了。
words.en: A trip is a journey in which you go somewhere, usually for a short time, and come back again.

words.ex: They went on a long voyage across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 他们进行了一次横跨海洋的长途航行。
words.en: A voyage is a long journey, especially by sea or in space.

words.ex: They went on a long journey by train.
words.ex_cn: 他们乘火车进行了一次长途旅行。
words.en: A journey is the act of traveling from one place to another, especially when this involves a long distance or a lot of time.

words.tr:
v. 航行；驾（船）；
n. 帆；航行；航海；
words.ex: They sail to the island every summer.
words.ex_cn: 他们每年夏天都乘船航行到那个岛。
words.en: To sail means to travel on water in a ship or boat, especially one that uses sails to catch the wind.

words.tr: n. 航海；帆船运动； v. 航行；“sail”的现在分词；
words.ex: He loves sailing on the open sea.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱在公海上航海。
words.en: The activity or sport of moving across water in a boat that is propelled by the wind.

words.tr: v. 导航；应付（复杂情况）；
words.ex: He uses a map to navigate the city.
words.ex_cn: 他用地图来导航这座城市。
words.en: To navigate is to plan and direct the route or course of a ship, aircraft, or other form of transport, especially by using instruments or maps.

words.ex: We went on an excursion to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山区进行了短途旅行。
words.en: An excursion is a short journey or trip, especially one taken as a leisure activity.

words.ex: We went to the beach during our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们在假期去了海滩。
words.en: A vacation is a period of time devoted to pleasure, rest, or relaxation, especially one with pay granted to an employee.

words.ex: The traffic on the highway was very heavy this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上高速公路上的交通非常拥堵。
words.en: Traffic refers to the movement of vehicles or people along roads, or to the movement of aircraft, ships, or trains. It can also refer to the trade or exchange of goods or services, especially illegal ones.

words.tr:
n. 火车；列车；列；队；
v. 训练；培训；
words.ex: I took the train to work this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上我坐火车去上班。
words.en: A train is a number of carriages or trucks which are all connected together and which are pulled by an engine along a railway. Train also means to teach someone the skills of a particular job or activity, or to be taught these skills.

words.tr:
n. 教练；长途客运汽车；
v. 训练；培训；
words.ex: The coach taught the team how to win.
words.ex_cn: 教练教球队如何获胜。
words.en: A coach is someone who trains a person or team in a particular sport. It also refers to a large, comfortable bus that carries passengers on long journeys.

words.ex: He takes the tram to work every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上乘电车上班。
words.en: A tram is a vehicle that is used for public transportation in cities and towns, running on tracks laid in the streets.

words.ex: The truck carried boxes to the store.
words.ex_cn: 卡车把箱子运到了商店。
words.en: A truck is a large vehicle that is used to transport goods by road.

words.ex: The lorry carried boxes to the warehouse.
words.ex_cn: 卡车把箱子运到了仓库。
words.en: A lorry is a large vehicle that is used to transport goods by road.

words.ex: The train runs on the railway.
words.ex_cn: 火车在铁路上行驶。
words.en: A track or set of tracks made of steel rails along which trains run for transporting passengers or goods.

words.ex: The car has four wheels.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有四个车轮。
words.en: A wheel is a circular object that revolves on an axle and is fixed below a vehicle or other object to enable it to move easily over the ground.

words.tr: n. 车辆；交通工具；媒介；
words.ex: The vehicle stopped at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在红灯前停了下来。
words.en: A vehicle is a machine such as a car, bus, or truck which has an engine and is used to carry people or goods from place to place.

words.tr:
v. 治疗；对待；
n. 款待；
words.ex: The doctor will treat his fever with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生会用药物治疗他的发烧。
words.en: If you treat someone or something in a particular way, you behave towards them or deal with them in that way.

words.ex: He showed me the trick to solve this math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他给我展示了快速解决这道数学题的诀窍。
words.en: A trick is a clever or deceitful action intended to deceive or outwit someone.

words.ex: I truly appreciate your help.
words.ex_cn: 我衷心感谢你的帮助。
words.en: You use truly to emphasize that something has all the features or qualities of a particular thing, or is the case to the fullest possible extent.

words.ex: The truth is that he was late for work.
words.ex_cn: 事实是他上班迟到了。
words.en: The truth is the true facts about something, rather than what is imagined or invented.

words.tr:
n. 曲调；调子；
v. 调整；调音；
words.ex: He hummed a happy tune while walking.
words.ex_cn: 他走路时哼着一首欢快的曲调。
words.en: A tune is a series of musical notes that are pleasant to listen to. It can also refer to adjusting something so that it works or looks better.

words.ex: He speaks Chinese as his mother tongue.
words.ex_cn: 他把汉语作为母语。
words.en: The tongue is the flexible muscular organ in the mouth that is used for tasting, licking, swallowing, and (in humans) articulating speech.

words.tr:
adj. 地下的；
n. 地铁；地下；
adv. 在地下；
words.ex: The underground tunnel connects two buildings.
words.ex_cn: 这条地下的隧道连接了两座建筑。
words.en: Something that is underground is below the surface of the ground. It can also refer to secret activities or organizations.

words.ex: The teacher underlined the key point.
words.ex_cn: 老师强调了这个关键点。
words.en: To draw a line under a word or phrase, especially in order to emphasize it.

words.ex: He finished his homework before the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 他在截止日期前完成了作业。
words.en: A deadline is a time or date before which a particular task must be finished or a particular thing must be done.

words.ex: The newspaper's headline said 'City Wins Championship'.
words.ex_cn: 报纸的大字标题写着‘城市赢得冠军’。
words.en: A headline is the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters at the top of the story, especially on the front page.

words.tr:
n. 轮廓；纲要；
v. 描画轮廓；概述；
words.ex: The artist drew the outline of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家画出了山的轮廓。
words.en: An outline is a line that shows or forms the outer edge of something, or a general description or plan showing the essential features of something but not the detail.

words.ex: He will undertake a new project next month.
words.ex_cn: 他下个月将从事一个新项目。
words.en: To undertake a task or job means to start doing it and accept responsibility for it.

words.ex: I clicked the button to undo my mistake.
words.ex_cn: 我点击了按钮来撤销我的错误。
words.en: To undo something means to reverse the effect of a previous action or to untie or unfasten something.

words.tr:
n. 折痕；褶；
v. 折叠；
words.ex: The paper has a deep fold in the middle.
words.ex_cn: 这张纸中间有一道深深的折痕。
words.en: To bend something, especially paper or cloth, so that one part of it lies flat on top of another part; to be able to be bent in this way.

words.ex: He unfolded the map on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他把地图在桌子上展开。
words.en: To open or spread out something that is folded; to develop or be revealed.

words.tr:
n. 皱纹
v. 起皱纹；弄皱…
words.ex: He has a deep wrinkle on his forehead.
words.ex_cn: 他的额头上有一道深深的皱纹。
words.en: A wrinkle is a small line or fold in something, especially fabric or the skin.

words.ex: The two teams decide to unite for the competition.
words.ex_cn: 这两个队伍决定在比赛中联合起来。
words.en: If a group of people or things unite or if someone unites them, they join together and act as a group.

words.ex: The two countries formed a union to strengthen trade.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家组成了一个联盟以加强贸易。
words.en: An organization of workers formed to protect their rights and interests; the act of joining two or more things together.

words.ex: This box weighs one unit.
words.ex_cn: 这个箱子重一单位。
words.en: A unit is a single thing or person that is part of something larger.

words.tr:
v. 力劝；
n. 强烈欲望；
words.ex: My teacher urged me to study harder.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师力劝我更加努力学习。
words.en: If you urge someone to do something, you try hard to persuade them to do it.

words.ex: The doctor said the patient needs urgent care.
words.ex_cn: 医生说病人需要紧急治疗。
words.en: If something is urgent, it needs to be dealt with as soon as possible.

words.ex: His answer was vague and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答不明确，难以理解。
words.en: If something written or spoken is vague, it does not explain or express things clearly.

words.tr:
n. 珍宝；宝物；财富；
v. 珍惜；
words.ex: The old map showed where the treasure was buried.
words.ex_cn: 那张旧地图显示了珍宝埋藏的地方。
words.en: If you treasure something that you have, you keep it or care for it carefully because it gives you great pleasure and you think it is very special.

words.tr:
n. 价值；（数）值；
v. 估价；重视；
words.ex: The value of this painting is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画的价值很高。
words.en: If you value something or someone, you think that they are important and you appreciate them.

words.tr: adj. 有价值的；贵重的；值钱的；
words.ex: This old book is valuable to historians.
words.ex_cn: 这本旧书对历史学家来说很有价值。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as valuable, you mean that they are very useful and helpful.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；非常宝贵的；
words.ex: Her advice was invaluable to me.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对我而言是无价的。
words.en: If you describe something as invaluable, you mean that it is extremely useful.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.tr:
v. 估算；估价；
n. 估价；估算；
words.ex: Can you estimate how long it will take?
words.ex_cn: 你能估算一下需要多长时间吗？
words.en: If you estimate a quantity or value, you make an approximate judgment or calculation of it.

words.ex: He underestimated the difficulty of the test.
words.ex_cn: 他低估了考试的难度。
words.en: If you underestimate something, you do not realize how large, great, or serious it is.

words.tr:
adj. 近似的；大约的；
v. 接近；
words.ex: The approximate cost is $50.
words.ex_cn: 费用大约是50美元。
words.en: An approximate number, time, or position is close to the correct number, time, or position, but is not exact.

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

words.ex: They have an intimate friendship.
words.ex_cn: 他们有着亲密的友谊。
words.en: having a close, friendly, or personal relationship with someone; private and personal

words.tr:
adj. 接近的；亲密的；
adv. 紧挨地；接近地；
v. 关闭；
words.ex: They are close friends.
words.ex_cn: 他们是亲密的朋友。
words.en: To move so as to bar passage through something; to shut.

words.tr: n. 重量；重物；重要性；负担；
words.ex: The weight of the box is 10 kilograms.
words.ex_cn: 这个箱子的重量是10公斤。
words.en: Weight is the force with which a body is attracted toward the earth or a celestial body by gravitation and which is equal to the product of the mass and the local gravitational acceleration.

words.ex: The doctor will weigh the baby at the clinic.
words.ex_cn: 医生将在诊所称量婴儿的体重。
words.en: To weigh something means to measure how heavy it is, usually by using scales. It can also mean to consider something carefully before making a decision.

words.ex: The heavy workload became a burden for her.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量成了她的负担。
words.en: A burden is a heavy load that is difficult to carry, or a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear.

words.ex: She sewed a button on her coat.
words.ex_cn: 她把一颗纽扣缝在了外套上。
words.en: A button is a small, usually round object that you press to operate a device or a machine, or a small, round object that you fasten to clothing to keep it closed.

words.ex: He fixed his collar before the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他在面试前整理了衣领。
words.en: The part of a piece of clothing that fits around the neck and is usually folded over; a band of material around the neck of an animal.

words.ex: She pulled the curtain to block the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 她拉上帷幕以挡住阳光。
words.en: A curtain is a piece of material that hangs down, often used to cover a window or to divide a room.

words.ex: The movie was tame and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影枯燥无味。
words.en: If you describe an animal as tame, you mean that it is not afraid of humans and is not dangerous. If you describe a person or their behavior as tame, you mean that they are not very exciting or interesting.

words.ex: The ice melts in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 冰在阳光下融化。
words.en: If a solid substance melts or if you melt it, it changes to a liquid, usually because it has been heated.

words.tr:
n. 度假胜地；手段；
v. 求助于；
words.ex: They went to a beach resort for their vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他们去一个海滨度假胜地度假。
words.en: If you resort to a particular course of action, you do it because you cannot see any other way of achieving what you want.

words.tr:
n. 种类；类别；
v. 理清；解决；把…分类；拣选；
words.ex: This store sells all sorts of fruits.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售各种各样的水果。
words.en: A sort is a kind or category of things or people which have similar characteristics.

words.tr:
n. 车费；费用；
v. 进展；成功（或不成功等）；
words.ex: The bus fare is two dollars.
words.ex_cn: 公交车费是两美元。
words.en: The fare is the amount of money that you pay for a journey that you make, for example, in a bus, train, or taxi.

words.ex: He said farewell to his friends before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他离开前向朋友们道别。
words.en: Farewell is an expression of good wishes at parting, often used to say goodbye.

words.ex: The government provides welfare to poor families.
words.ex_cn: 政府向贫困家庭提供福利。
words.en: The welfare of a person or group is their health, comfort, and happiness.

words.tr: n. 奖金；红利；额外津贴；
words.ex: He received a bonus for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了奖金。
words.en: A bonus is an extra amount of money that is added to someone's pay, usually because they have worked very hard.

words.tr: n. 养老金；退休金；抚恤金；
words.ex: He receives a monthly pension after retiring.
words.ex_cn: 他退休后每月领取养老金。
words.en: A pension is a sum of money which a retired, widowed, or disabled person regularly receives from the state or from a former employer.

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.tr: v. 允许；留出；给予；承认；
words.ex: My parents allow me to go out on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 我的父母允许我周末外出。
words.en: If someone is allowed to do something, it is all right for them to do it and they will not get into trouble.

words.tr: adj. 愿意的；乐意的； v. “will”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is willing to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他愿意帮助他的朋友。
words.en: If someone is willing to do something, they are happy to do it if it is needed.

words.tr:
n. 志愿者；
v. 自愿做；
words.ex: He is a volunteer at the local hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地医院的一名志愿者。
words.en: A volunteer is someone who does work without being paid for it, especially work that involves helping people.

words.tr:
n. 风；
v. 缠绕；蜿蜒；
words.ex: The wind blew strongly through the trees.
words.ex_cn: 风猛烈地吹过树木。
words.en: Wind is the natural movement of air, especially in the form of a current of air blowing from a particular direction.

words.tr:
v. 抗议；
n. 抗议活动；
words.ex: The students protest against the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 学生们抗议新的校规。
words.en: A protest is the act of saying or showing publicly that you object to something.

words.ex: He won the spelling contest.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了拼写比赛。
words.en: A contest is a competition or a struggle for victory between individuals or groups.

words.ex: He detests eating broccoli.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌吃西兰花。
words.en: If you detest something, you dislike it intensely.

words.ex: The students participated in a history quiz at school.
words.ex_cn: 学生们参加了学校举办的历史知识竞赛。
words.en: A quiz is a test or a game in which someone asks you questions to find out how much you know about a subject.

words.ex: He solved the crossword puzzle quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快解开了这个填字谜。
words.en: If something puzzles you, you do not understand it and feel confused.

words.ex: The teacher gave us a questionnaire about our habits.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我们一份关于我们习惯的问卷。
words.en: A questionnaire is a written list of questions which are answered by a lot of people in order to provide information for a report or a survey.

words.tr:
n. 谜语；费解的事
v. 解谜；出谜；使布满窟窿；打洞
words.ex: He told me a riddle and I solved it.
words.ex_cn: 他给我出了一道谜语，我解出来了。
words.en: A riddle is a question or statement that is deliberately very confusing and has a clever or amusing answer.

words.ex: I assume it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假定明天会下雨。
words.en: If you assume that something is true, you accept that it is true without proof.

words.ex: I presume he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假设他明天会到。
words.en: If you presume that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you are not certain.

words.ex: After a short break, he resumed his work.
words.ex_cn: 短暂休息后，他继续工作。
words.en: If you resume an activity or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after an interruption.

words.ex: The child recites the poem every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子每天早上背诵这首诗。
words.en: To repeat aloud or declaim (a poem or passage) from memory before an audience.

words.ex: The car consumes a lot of gas.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车消耗很多汽油。
words.en: To consume something means to eat or drink it, or to use it up in some way.

words.ex: In this village, it is a custom to light lanterns during the festival.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村庄，节日期间点灯笼是一种习俗。
words.en: A custom is an activity, a way of behaving, or an event which is usual or traditional in a particular society or in particular circumstances.

words.ex: The customer bought a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 这位客户买了一部新手机。
words.en: A customer is someone who buys goods or services from a shop or business.

words.tr: n. 习俗；习惯；关税；海关；“custom”的复数；
words.ex: In this village, it is a custom to light lanterns during the festival.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村庄，节日里点灯笼是一种习俗。
words.en: The place at a port, airport, or border where officials check the goods or luggage of people entering or leaving a country, and where they collect taxes on goods being imported.

words.ex: He wants to pursue his dream of becoming a writer.
words.ex_cn: 他想追求成为作家的梦想。
words.en: If you pursue an activity, interest, or plan, you carry it out or follow it.

words.tr:
n. 购买；采购；
v. 购买；采购；
words.ex: The purchase of a new car took all his savings.
words.ex_cn: 买一辆新车花光了他所有的积蓄。
words.en: To purchase something means to buy it. It can also refer to something that has been bought.

words.tr: n. 女用小包；钱包；资金；
words.ex: She put her keys in her purse.
words.ex_cn: 她把钥匙放进她的女用小包里。
words.en: A purse is a small bag used especially by women to carry everyday personal items.

words.tr: v. 买得起；担负得起；有时间做；
words.ex: I can't afford a new car.
words.ex_cn: 我买不起一辆新车。
words.en: If you cannot afford something, you do not have enough money to pay for it.

words.ex: He works hard to earn money.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以赚取收入。
words.en: To earn means to gain something, especially money or respect, through your own efforts or work.

words.tr: v. 发芽；长出；迅速成长；涌现；
words.ex: The seed will sprout in spring.
words.ex_cn: 这颗种子会在春天发芽。
words.en: If a plant sprouts, or if it sprouts something, it produces new leaves or buds.

words.tr:
v. 分开；分裂；
n. 划分；分歧；
words.ex: The tree split in the storm.
words.ex_cn: 那棵树在风暴中裂开了。
words.en: If something splits or if you split it, it is divided into two or more parts.

words.tr:
v. 喷吐；吐痰；吐口水
n. 唾沫；一块陆地；烤肉叉
words.ex: He likes to spit watermelon seeds.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢吐西瓜籽。
words.en: To spit means to force out the contents of the mouth, especially saliva, through the lips. It can also refer to the act of ejecting saliva or phlegm from the mouth, often as a gesture of contempt or disrespect.

words.tr:
v. 溢出；溅出
n. 溢出；溅出
words.ex: He spilled milk on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 他把牛奶洒在了地上。
words.en: To cause or allow (a liquid, powder, etc.) to flow or fall out of a container, usually by accident.

words.tr:
n. 幻灯片；滑梯；
v. （使）滑动；下滑；
words.ex: He showed a slide of his vacation photos.
words.ex_cn: 他展示了一张他度假照片的幻灯片。
words.en: To move smoothly along a surface while maintaining continuous contact with it; to pass or move quietly or smoothly; a structure with a smooth sloping surface for children to slide down; a decline from a higher to a lower level or status.

words.tr: n. 切片；薄片；部分；片段；
words.ex: She ate a slice of bread for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 她早餐吃了一片面包。
words.en: A slice of something is a thin piece or portion of it.

words.tr: adj. 苗条的；纤细的；微小的；
words.ex: She has a slim figure.
words.ex_cn: 她身材苗条。
words.en: If someone is slim, they are thin in an attractive way.

words.tr:
n. 纸片；
v. 滑倒；溜走；
words.ex: She found a slip of paper on the table.
words.ex_cn: 她在桌子上发现了一张纸片。
words.en: If you slip, you accidentally slide and lose your balance.

words.ex: He skipped the hard question and moved to the next one.
words.ex_cn: 他略过了难题，继续做下一题。
words.en: To move lightly and quickly, making a small jump after each step.

words.ex: The children played on the slope behind the house.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房子后面的斜坡上玩耍。
words.en: A slope is a surface that is at an angle, so that one end is higher than the other.

words.tr: adj. 陡峭的；急剧升降的；
words.ex: The mountain has a steep path.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一条陡峭的小路。
words.en: A steep slope or hill is one that is at a sharp angle, rather than being flat or gradual.

words.tr:
n. 步；步骤；踏级；步伐；
v. 踩；踏；行走；
words.ex: He took a small step forward.
words.ex_cn: 他向前迈了一小步。
words.en: A step is an act or movement of putting one leg in front of the other in order to move forward, or a stage in a process.

words.ex: He changed his pace to match the group.
words.ex_cn: 他调整了步伐以跟上队伍。
words.en: The speed at which someone or something moves, or with which something happens or changes.

words.ex: He showed patience while waiting for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他在等公交车时表现出了耐心。
words.en: The ability to stay calm and not get angry, especially when there is a difficulty or you have to wait a long time.

words.tr:
n. 病人；
adj. 有耐心的；
words.ex: The doctor helped the patient feel better.
words.ex_cn: 医生帮助病人感觉好些了。
words.en: A patient person is able to wait for a long time or deal with a difficult situation without becoming angry or upset.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.tr:
v. 喂；吃；
n. 饲养；喂养；
words.ex: She feeds the cat every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上喂猫。
words.en: To give food to a person or an animal; to supply something to a machine or a system.

words.tr:
n. 营地；
v. 宿营；露营；
words.ex: The children set up a camp near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在湖边搭了一个营地。
words.en: A camp is a place where people live temporarily in tents or other temporary structures.

words.ex: He walks to class on campus every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上步行到校园上课。
words.en: The grounds and buildings of a university or college.

words.tr: n. （政治、商业或社会性）活动；运动；
words.ex: The city launched a campaign to reduce plastic waste.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市发起了一项减少塑料垃圾的活动。
words.en: A campaign is a planned set of activities that people carry out over a period of time in order to achieve something such as social or political change.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.ex: They slept in a tent during the camping trip.
words.ex_cn: 他们在露营时睡在帐篷里。
words.en: A tent is a portable shelter made of fabric or other material stretched over a supporting framework of poles and usually stabilized or secured to the ground with cords and stakes.

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

words.tr:
n. 内容；含量；
adj. 满足的；
words.ex: The content of the video is very interesting.
words.ex_cn: 这个视频的内容非常有趣。
words.en: Content refers to the things that are held or included in something, or the state of being happy and satisfied.

words.ex: The teacher gave extra praise to satisfy the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师给予额外的表扬来使学生满意。
words.en: If someone or something satisfies you, they give you enough of what you want or need to make you pleased or contented.

words.ex: He felt satisfaction after finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他完成作业后感到满意。
words.en: The feeling of pleasure that you have when you do or get something that you wanted or needed.

words.ex: They will liberate the prisoners tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天会释放这些囚犯。
words.en: To liberate a place or the people in it means to free them from the political or military control of another country, area, or group of people.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.ex: The slave worked in the fields every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个奴隶每天在田地里劳作。
words.en: A slave is someone who is the legal property of another person and is forced to obey them.

words.tr:
n. 劳动；体力劳动；劳工；
v. 辛勤工作；
words.ex: Hard labour helps people build strong skills.
words.ex_cn: 辛勤的劳动帮助人们培养强大的技能。
words.en: Labour is very hard work, especially physical work. It can also refer to the workers of a country or industry, considered as a group, or the process of childbirth.

words.tr:
n. 形式；表格；形状；
v. 组成；建立；
words.ex: The form of the poem is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的形式非常简单。
words.en: A form is a particular way in which a thing exists or appears, or a document with spaces in which to write information.

words.tr:
adj. 一致的；统一的；
n. 制服；
words.ex: The students wear a uniform shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 学生们穿一致的衬衫去学校。
words.en: A uniform is a special set of clothes which some people, for example soldiers or the police, wear to work in and which some children wear at school. It is also used to describe something that is the same in all parts and does not vary.

words.ex: The government announced a major reform in education.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布了教育方面的重大改革。
words.en: If someone reforms a system, they change or improve it.

words.ex: He will perform the task tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会执行这个任务。
words.en: To perform means to carry out, accomplish, or fulfill an action, task, or function. It can also refer to the act of presenting a form of entertainment, such as a play, concert, or other artistic expression, before an audience.

words.tr:
n. 格式；
v. 格式化；
words.ex: The file is in PDF format.
words.ex_cn: 这个文件是PDF格式。
words.en: The way in which something is arranged or set out.

words.ex: The teacher stood on the platform to speak.
words.ex_cn: 老师站在平台上讲话。
words.en: A platform is a flat, raised structure, usually made of wood, which people stand on when they make speeches or give performances.

words.ex: He wore a formal suit to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一套正式的西装去参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is formal is done or said according to an established or conventional way, especially in an official or serious situation.

words.tr:
n. 官员；高级职员；
adj. 官方的；正式的；
words.ex: The official announced new rules for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 这位官员宣布了节日的新规定。
words.en: An official is a person who holds a position of authority in a government or organization, or something that is authorized or formally recognized.

words.ex: The officer gave a clear order to the soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 军官向士兵下达了明确的命令。
words.en: An officer is a person in a position of authority in the armed forces, the police, or a government organization.

words.tr: adj. 随意的；非正式的；偶然的；
words.ex: He wore casual clothes to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了随意的衣服去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe someone's attitude or behavior as casual, you mean they are not very concerned about what they are doing or what is happening around them, or they are not taking it seriously.

words.tr:
n. 公司；商行；
adj. 坚固的；结实的；
words.ex: He works for a small firm in London.
words.ex_cn: 他在伦敦一家小公司工作。
words.en: If something is firm, it does not change much in shape when it is pressed but is not completely hard. A firm is an organization which sells or produces something or which provides a service which people pay for.

words.ex: The test results confirm he has the disease.
words.ex_cn: 检测结果证实他患有这种疾病。
words.en: To confirm something means to establish its truth or validity by providing evidence or proof.

words.ex: Please inform me when the meeting starts.
words.ex_cn: 请在会议开始时通知我。
words.en: To inform someone means to tell them about something.

words.ex: The new teacher transformed the class into a lively group.
words.ex_cn: 这位新老师把班级变成了一个充满活力的团体。
words.en: To transform something or someone means to change them completely and usually improve their appearance, form, or structure.

words.ex: He can translate words into pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他能把词语转化为图画。
words.en: To translate means to change written or spoken words from one language into another, or to explain something in a way that is easier to understand.

words.ex: The translation of the book took two months.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的翻译花了两个月。
words.en: The process of translating words or text from one language into another.

words.ex: The glass is transparent.
words.ex_cn: 这玻璃是透明的。
words.en: If something is transparent, you can see through it.

words.tr:
n. 运输；
v. 运输；
words.ex: He uses public transport to go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐公共交通去上班。
words.en: To transport something or someone is to move them from one place to another, especially over long distances.

words.tr:
v. 移栽；移植；
n. 移植；
words.ex: He will transplant the flowers to the garden tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要把这些花移栽到花园里。
words.en: To transplant something means to move it from one place to another. In medicine, to transplant an organ, piece of skin, etc. means to use it to replace a damaged part in someone's body.

words.ex: The radio transmits music to listeners.
words.ex_cn: 收音机将音乐传递给听众。
words.en: To send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another.

words.ex: He finally admit his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他终于承认了自己的错误。
words.en: If you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, you agree, often unwillingly, that it is true.

words.tr:
n. 许可证；
v. 允许；准许；
words.ex: He showed his fishing permit to the officer.
words.ex_cn: 他向官员出示了他的钓鱼许可证。
words.en: If someone permits something, they allow it to happen. If they permit you to do something, they allow you to do it.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.tr:
v. 错过；想念；漏掉；
n. 小姐；
words.ex: I missed the bus this morning.
words.ex_cn: 我今天早上错过了公交车。
words.en: To fail to hit, reach, catch, or otherwise make contact with something; to feel the absence or loss of someone or something.

words.ex: The army launched a missile at the target.
words.ex_cn: 军队向目标发射了一枚导弹。
words.en: A missile is a weapon that is sent through the air and that explodes when it hits the thing it is aimed at.

words.ex: He omitted the last word in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他省略了句子中的最后一个词。
words.en: If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.

words.ex: The lamp emits a soft light.
words.ex_cn: 灯发出柔和的光。
words.en: To emit means to send out something such as light, heat, sound, gas, etc.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.tr: v. 承诺；犯（罪、错）；（公开地）表达意见；
words.ex: He commit to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺帮助他的朋友。
words.en: To commit means to carry out or perpetrate a mistake, crime, or immoral act; or to pledge or bind oneself to a certain course of action.

words.ex: He made a commitment to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他承诺按时完成这个项目。
words.en: A commitment is something that regularly takes up some of your time because of an agreement you have made or because of responsibilities that you have.

words.ex: The committee meets every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 委员会每周一开会。
words.en: A committee is a group of people who are chosen to do a particular job or make decisions on behalf of a larger group.

words.ex: The weather bureau issued a storm warning.
words.ex_cn: 气象局发布了风暴预警。
words.en: A bureau is an office, organization, or government department that collects and distributes information.
